1: The average kinetic energy is proportional to the absolute temperature because zero kelvin is the temperature where the motion stops. Using Celsius would give a wrong ratio, so always convert to kelvin.
2: Mass and energy are equivalent, so any energy change corresponds to a mass change Δm = ΔE/c². This is why nuclear reactions show a measurable mass difference.
3: A bound nucleus has less mass than its separate nucleons, and the difference is the mass defect. The energy equivalent of that mass is the binding energy, which is released when the nucleus forms.
4: Binding energy per nucleon peaks near iron-56, so the most stable nuclei lie there. Fusion of light nuclei and fission of heavy nuclei both move towards that peak and release energy.
